subject: [Clearwave] model-8q-rc2 p95 spike — request for rollback clearance
messages:
From: Lina Torres <lina@clearwave.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: salesops@clearwave.com
Date: Fri, 05 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p95 spike on model-8q-rc2 in prod (Oct 5)

Hi Connor,

We started seeing a p95 latency spike around 08:45 PT after the rollout of model-8q-rc2 to our production route. The impact is visible in our user-facing inference calls: p95 jumped from ~350ms to ~1.6s for the last 30 minutes. Throughput and error rates look normal but end-user sessions are timing out occasionally.

Attached is a quick view from our dashboard (p95_chart_20281005.png). Can you confirm whether you have an automated rollback threshold for this variant, or if we need to request a manual rollback? This is impacting a small subset of high-frequency routes — happy to share traffic sample if it helps.

Thanks,
Lina
Lina Torres
Director, Platform Integrations
Clearwave Tech
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lina Torres <lina@clearwave.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Oct 2028 09:35:24 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Sudden p95 spike on model-8q-rc2 in prod (Oct 5)

Team — forwarding Clearwave's report. They observe a sustained p95 jump to ~1.6s after rc2 rollout. Internal monitoring has a soft alert but no automated rollback triggered (thresholds set conservatively for this stage).

TL;DR: customer-facing latency spike; request: authorization to perform an immediate rollback of model-8q-rc2 on Clearwave's dedicated route, or approval for a temporary SLA carveout while we isolate root cause.

Observed from our telemetry so far:
- p50 stable (~120ms)
- p95 elevated (~1.5–1.8s) for the last 25 minutes
- no elevated 5xx errors
- KV cache hit-rate unchanged

Proposed next steps:
1) Grant rollback clearance (30-min window) and schedule rollback at 10:00 PT if approved.
2) If rollback not approved, authorize a short SLA grace period and fail open to model-7x (pre-rc) fallback routing.

I've attached our rollback playbook (rollback_playbook_model-8q.pdf) and a quick p95 snapshot. Markus — can you run a quick canary artifact check (kernel selection / allreduce changes in rc2)? Naomi — please advise on contract/SLA implications if we trigger a rollback.

Connor
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Lina Torres <lina@clearwave.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Oct 2028 10:01:08 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden p95 spike on model-8q-rc2 in prod (Oct 5)

Quick forensic note: rc2 introduced a kernel fallback path for long-sequence attention that interacts poorly with our dynamic batching heuristics for their traffic shape. Local replay of Clearwave sample traffic reproduces the p95 increase; p50 unaffected. Root cause likely increased tail latency on the attention kernel under certain batch compositions.

Mitigation options:
- Immediate: rollback rc2 for Clearwave's route (fastest, lowest risk).
- Short term: enable strict batching caps (reduces throughput) and set fallback to model-7x for high-concurrency sessions.
- Long term: patch kernel code and re-qualify rc2 (2–3 day turnaround).

I recommend rollback. If leadership approves, I can coordinate with infra to execute a controlled rollback at 10:00 PT and monitor p95 for 30 minutes post-rollback.

Markus
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lina Torres <lina@clearwave.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Oct 2028 11:12:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden p95 spike on model-8q-rc2 in prod (Oct 5) — rollback clearance

Connor / Markus — thanks for the rapid triage. Given the reproduced tail behavior and the customer's live impact, I authorize an immediate rollback for Clearwave's prod route. Conditions:
- Perform rollback between 10:00–10:30 PT today (earlier is fine if infra can move faster).
- Notify Clearwave of the planned 10:00 PT rollback and confirmation window.
- Naomi, please confirm any contractual notification obligations — we want to avoid a formal SLA credit if we can remediate within the window.
- Post-rollback, capture p50/p95/time-to-stable metrics and reopen RC2 only after a full patch & re-qualification.

Marissa
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Torres <lina@clearwave.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 06 Oct 2028 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 spike on model-8q-rc2 in prod (Oct 5) — scheduled rollback executed

Hi Lina — quick status: per approved plan, we rolled back model-8q-rc2 on your prod route at 10:03 PT this morning. Markus and infra observed p95 drop back to ~330ms within five minutes and system stabilized within the 30-minute window.

Deliverables:
- Rollback executed: 2028-10-06 10:03 PT
- Immediate result: p95 returned to expected baseline (~320–360ms)
- Follow-up: Markus will open INF-3421 with the kernel repro notes and target a patched rc2 by EOW next week; Naomi will follow up about whether a customer-facing SLA credit is needed after we review the impact window.

Thanks for flagging this quickly — we will keep you updated on the remediation timeline.

Connor O'Brien
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
